CLAUDE_DEV_SSH_PORT.description: Host port the dev container's SSH server listens on. The operator port-forwards this on the FritzBox (or reaches it over the LAN) to attach the Claude Code mobile app. Default 2222 so it stays clear of the host's own sshd on 22.

CLAUDE_DEV_SSH_PASSWORD.description: Password for the `dev` SSH user. Auto-generated and surfaced as a credential after install. Used to attach over SSH when no public key is supplied. Regenerate from the wizard if it leaks.

CLAUDE_DEV_SSH_AUTHORIZED_KEY.description: Optional SSH public key (one line, e.g. `ssh-ed25519 AAAA... you@phone`). When set, key-based login is enabled for the `dev` user — recommended over the password for a box reachable from outside the LAN. Leave blank to use the password only.

CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN.description: Optional long-lived Claude subscription token, so the auto-started Claude sessions never need an interactive /login. Generate it once on any machine that has a browser with `claude setup-token` — it is account-scoped, not machine-scoped, so the token from your laptop works here. Leave blank to keep the interactive login, whose refresh token carries a rolling ~30-day expiry and must then be re-entered by hand in every tmux window (impractical from the mobile app). `noAutoGenerate` is load-bearing: this is an operator-supplied external credential, and a random string minted in its place would be rejected on every API call.

SERVICEBAY_MCP_TOKEN.description: ServiceBay API token, so every Claude session on this box can read ADRs, assists, logs and rendered service definitions without one being pasted in by hand. Leave blank and ServiceBay mints one for you at install: READ scope only, never expiring — the combination it offers exclusively for read-only scope sets, which is why this one is safe to generate and needs no rotation. A session that needs to restart or deploy something calls `request_token` (which itself needs only `read`) and you approve that one job; a shell goes through the one-shot flow bound to a single operation. Paste your own token here to use it instead — an operator-supplied value always wins over the generated one. One shared token is deliberate: the scope ladder has no per-service granularity, so per-repo tokens would buy attribution and nothing else.

CLAUDE_DEV_CONFIG_PORT.description: Port the container's own configuration UI listens on. Published on the host's 127.0.0.1 only, so the reverse proxy is the single way in — nothing on the LAN can reach it directly and skip the sign-in. Change it only if 8790 is already taken on this box.

CLAUDE_DEV_CONFIG_SUBDOMAIN.description: Subdomain for the claude-dev configuration UI, e.g. `claude.<your domain>`. This is the dev box's own configuration, so it is an ADMIN surface: the auth template's access_control table names `claude.<domain>` in its admins-only rule and in the explicit-deny twin, so a household `family` account is refused rather than passed through the wildcard (#2936). The UI then independently refuses anyone outside CLAUDE_DEV_LDAP_GROUP, so a group change on the dev box narrows access further but can never widen it past the admins group.

CLAUDE_DEV_PI_PORT.description: Port the container's pi web chat (pi-web-ui) listens on. Published on the host's 127.0.0.1 only, so the reverse proxy and the sign-in are the single way in. Deliberately NOT pi-web-ui's own default of 8787 — that port is already taken on this box by solaris. Change it only if 8791 is taken too.

CLAUDE_DEV_PI_SUBDOMAIN.description: Subdomain for the pi web chat, e.g. `pi.<your domain>` — the second agent in this container, alongside the Claude sessions you reach over SSH and Remote Control. Authelia is the ONLY gate here: pi-web-ui carries no sign-in of its own and hands whoever reaches it an interactive agent with a bash tool running as `dev` inside this container. So this is an ADMIN surface — the auth template names `pi.<domain>` in its admins-only two-factor rule and in the explicit-deny twin, and a household `family` account is refused (#2936). Never point this subdomain at a port that is reachable without the proxy, and never move the host out of that rule.

CLAUDE_DEV_PI_MODEL_BASE_URL.description: The OpenAI-compatible endpoint pi talks to — this box's own local model server. It is the only model source this template configures: no cloud provider, no API key, no OAuth. The default points at the solarisbay `llama` template's llama-server (its `LLAMA_PORT`, 11435). That listener has to be reachable from an isolated pod, which lands with mdopp/solarisbay#1344 — until then nothing answers here and pi's model picker stays empty. `host.containers.internal` is how an isolated pod reaches an on-box sibling (ADR 0007); `localhost` would be this pod's own loopback and a LAN IP is refused outright by rootless podman. Change the port here if your model server listens elsewhere.

CLAUDE_DEV_PI_MODEL_ID.description: Optional: the model id to offer in pi, e.g. what `curl <CLAUDE_DEV_PI_MODEL_BASE_URL>/models` reports. Comma-separate several. Leave blank and the container asks the model server itself at start-up and writes back whatever it lists — set this only when the server is not up at deploy time or you want to pin one model.

LLDAP_LDAP_PORT.description: LLDAP LDAP-protocol port. Must match the `auth` stack's LLDAP_LDAP_PORT.

LLDAP_BASE_DN.description: LDAP base DN, e.g. dc=example,dc=com. Must match the `auth` stack's LLDAP_BASE_DN — leave blank and ServiceBay derives the same value from PUBLIC_DOMAIN at install time. Users resolve under ou=people, groups under ou=groups.

LLDAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD.description: LLDAP admin bind password. Not asked for here — reused automatically from the value the `auth` stack generated (savedSecrets is keyed by variable name). When empty (auth never installed) LDAP login is skipped and only the local `dev` account works.

CLAUDE_DEV_LDAP_GROUP.description: Only LLDAP users in this group may SSH in, and only they may open the configuration UI at CLAUDE_DEV_CONFIG_SUBDOMAIN. Defaults to `admins`, the group your operator account belongs to. The entrypoint provisions a local login account for each member of this group; point it at a dedicated group to grant dev-box access without making someone a full admin. It does NOT gate the pi web chat: pi has no group check of its own, so `pi.<domain>` is held by the auth template's admins-only access_control rule instead (#2936). Pointing this at a non-admin group therefore widens SSH and the configuration UI, never the web surfaces — those stay admins-only until the auth template's rule says otherwise.
